desc:
You are given a string s of lowercase letters and two scores x and y. You may repeatedly perform either of these operations as long as they apply:

  • delete a substring 'ab' and earn x points;
  • delete a substring 'ba' and earn y points.

After each deletion the two remaining sides join. Return the maximum total number of points you can earn.

Example: s = 'cdbcbbaaabab', x = 4, y = 5 gives 19.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Removing one pair can destroy or create other pairs, so the order matters. Try small strings such as 'aba' by hand to see why.
Only the letters a and b matter, and any other letter separates the string into independent parts. Is it better to remove the more valuable pair first or last?
Remove all pairs of the more valuable kind first, using a stack, then remove all pairs of the other kind from what is left. Add up the points.
editorial: Suppose x ≥ y (otherwise swap the roles). Greedy claim: remove every possible 'ab' first, then every possible 'ba'. Each removal uses up one a and one b, and a pair of the cheaper kind that is removed early can destroy at most one pair of the dearer kind, so an exchange argument shows that taking dearer pairs first never loses points. Letters other than a and b are never removed and just act as walls.

Implement each pass with a stack: for the first pass push characters and whenever the top is a and the incoming character is b, pop and add x. The characters left in the stack form the string for the second pass, in which the pair 'ba' is removed the same way and y is added. Each pass is linear, so the total time is O(n) and the space O(n).
